back: A sudden shaking of the ground caused by the release of stress when rocks break or slip along a fault.
The point underground where an earthquake starts.
The point on the surface directly above the focus; shaking is usually strongest here.
P waves (fastest, push-pull, solids and liquids), S waves (slower, side to side, solids only), surface waves (slowest, most damage).
Magnitude (Richter, moment magnitude): energy released, one value, logarithmic. Intensity (Mercalli I-XII): effects at a place, varies with distance.
Each whole step is 10 times the ground movement and about 32 times the energy.
Tsunamis, liquefaction, landslides and fires; often deadlier than the shaking itself.
Linked to the East African Rift (e.g. central Mozambique, 2006, magnitude about 7), faults, Lake Kariba (reservoir-induced) and deep mining in South Africa.
An instrument that detects and records ground movement; the record is a seismogram.
